Then D=W^-1 U dom H^(1/2) is a graph core disjoint from dom H. For T=H^(1/2)|D, T*=closure T=H^(1/2), dom T*T=D∩dom H={0} whereas closure T* closure T=H. If H is bounded, closure T bounded, so T* everywhere and dom T*T=dom T, not zero. All eigenvalue/continuous spectrum cases covered.

originality.rationale: The 2026 source proves existence without a prescribed closed product; Arlinskiĭ–Zagrebnov 2015 prove substantial disjoint-domain and closed proper-restriction theorems but not this single graph-dense core construction preserving an arbitrary given H exactly. The classical von Neumann unitary is the cited nonoriginal input. Searches of research records and primary source sections showed no directly covering statement; equivalence in older domain literature remains a residual publication risk.
residual_risks: The von Neumann unitary is a powerful old theorem; the graph-space transfer and exact product-prescription may have appeared as an unindexed equivalent corollary.
Only relevant parts, not the full original corpus, of Arlinskiĭ–Zagrebnov were examined; older operator-domain papers could use different terminology.
The Dehimi–Mortad full text was not inspected; its abstract has an essentially-selfadjoint trivial-square example but does not assert universality.

value.rationale: A complete classification for preassigned nonnegative selfadjoint operators: unboundedness alone is necessary and sufficient for an essentially selfadjoint representing core with trivial adjoint-product domain but exactly the specified closed product. This preserves arbitrary spectral type and multiplicity, clarifying the gap between closure of forms and products in the motivating 2026 literature. The classical nontrivial unitary theorem is credited; no claim of a new proof of that lemma.
